subject: Applied Calculus
unit: Unit II — Functions of Several Variables

sourceBasis.syllabus: R-2025 Unit II: partial derivatives, chain rule, total derivative, maxima/minima of two variables, Lagrange multipliers and engineering applications.

note: Original ACADRIX 1-mark practice questions; not claimed official Anna University questions or verified PYQs.

questions.q: What is a function of two variables?
questions.a: A function z=f(x,y) that assigns one output z to each permitted ordered pair (x,y).

questions.q: What represents the domain of a function of two variables?
questions.a: A region of permitted ordered pairs in the xy-plane.

questions.q: What is a partial derivative?
questions.a: The derivative with respect to one variable while the other independent variables are held constant.

questions.q: What does fₓ denote?
What does fᵧ denote?
When finding fₓ, how is y treated?
questions.a: As a constant.

questions.q: When finding fᵧ, how is x treated?
questions.a: As a constant.

questions.q: What is a higher-order partial derivative?
questions.a: A partial derivative obtained by differentiating a partial derivative again.

questions.q: What does fₓₓ represent?
questions.a: The second partial derivative with respect to x.

questions.q: What does fᵧᵧ represent?
questions.a: The second partial derivative with respect to y.

questions.q: What is a mixed partial derivative?
questions.a: A partial derivative obtained by differentiating with respect to different variables successively.

questions.q: What does fₓᵧ represent?
questions.a: Differentiate f first with respect to x and then with respect to y, according to the notation convention used.

questions.q: Under what type of condition are mixed partial derivatives equal?
questions.a: Under appropriate continuity conditions on the relevant second partial derivatives.

questions.q: For z=f(x,y), x=x(t), and y=y(t), state the multivariable chain rule for dz/dt.
questions.a: dz/dt=fₓ(dx/dt)+fᵧ(dy/dt).

questions.q: What is the purpose of the multivariable chain rule?
questions.a: To account for all paths through which changing intermediate variables affects the dependent variable.

questions.q: Write the total differential of z=f(x,y).
questions.a: dz=fₓdx+fᵧdy.

questions.q: What does the total differential represent?
questions.a: The first-order change in z due to small simultaneous changes in x and y.

questions.q: What is meant by a stationary point of a function of two variables?
questions.a: An interior point where fₓ=0 and fᵧ=0.

questions.q: What equations are solved to find interior stationary points?
questions.a: fₓ=0 and fᵧ=0.

questions.q: Write the two-variable second-derivative discriminant D.
questions.a: D=fₓₓfᵧᵧ−(fₓᵧ)².

questions.q: What is the classification when D>0 and fₓₓ>0?
questions.a: Local minimum.

questions.q: What is the classification when D>0 and fₓₓ<0?
questions.a: Local maximum.

questions.q: What does D<0 indicate at a stationary point?
questions.a: A saddle point.

questions.q: What does D=0 indicate in the two-variable second-derivative test?
questions.a: The test is inconclusive.

questions.q: What is a saddle point?
questions.a: A stationary point that is neither a local maximum nor a local minimum, classified by D<0 in this test.

questions.q: What is a local maximum of a function of two variables?
questions.a: A point where the function has a locally greatest value compared with nearby domain points.

questions.q: What is a local minimum of a function of two variables?
questions.a: A point where the function has a locally least value compared with nearby domain points.

questions.q: What is the first main step in classifying stationary points?
questions.a: Find fₓ and fᵧ and solve fₓ=0 and fᵧ=0.

questions.q: Which second partial derivatives are needed for the discriminant D?
questions.a: fₓₓ, fᵧᵧ and fₓᵧ.

questions.q: What is a constraint in an optimisation problem?
questions.a: A condition or equation restricting the allowable values of the variables.

questions.q: What is the Lagrange multiplier method used for?
questions.a: Finding maxima or minima of an objective function subject to a constraint.

questions.q: State the Lagrange multiplier condition for f subject to g(x,y)=c.
questions.a: ∇f=λ∇g.

questions.q: Write the x-component Lagrange equation.
questions.a: fₓ=λgₓ.

questions.q: Write the y-component Lagrange equation.
questions.a: fᵧ=λgᵧ.

questions.q: What additional equation must be used with the Lagrange equations?
questions.a: The constraint g(x,y)=c.

questions.q: What does λ represent in the Lagrange multiplier method?
questions.a: A scalar multiplier introduced to enforce the constraint in the stationarity condition.

questions.q: What is ∇f called?
questions.a: The gradient of f.

questions.q: For f(x,y), what are the components of ∇f?
questions.a: fₓ and fᵧ, so ∇f=(fₓ,fᵧ).

questions.q: Give one engineering use of partial derivatives.
questions.a: Studying temperature variation with position.

questions.q: Give one engineering use of multivariable optimisation.
questions.a: Optimising dimensions for minimum material or maximum performance.

questions.q: What kind of engineering response can be represented by z=f(x,y)?
questions.a: A response depending simultaneously on two variables such as position, temperature, pressure or dimensions.

questions.q: If f=x²y+3y², what is fₓ?
questions.a: 2xy.

questions.q: If f=x²y+3y², what is fᵧ?
questions.a: x²+6y.

questions.q: If z=f(x,y), what does dx/dt describe?
questions.a: The rate of change of x with respect to t.

questions.q: If z=f(x,y), what does dy/dt describe?
questions.a: The rate of change of y with respect to t.

questions.q: Why can partial derivatives be useful in engineering design?
questions.a: They quantify how a response changes with one design variable while other variables are held fixed.

questions.q: What should be calculated after finding stationary points for the standard two-variable classification test?
questions.a: The second partial derivatives and D.

questions.q: What is the main difference between an unconstrained and constrained optimisation problem?
questions.a: A constrained problem includes one or more conditions restricting the variables.

questions.q: What is meant by total derivative when dependent variables change simultaneously?
questions.a: It accounts for the combined effect of the changing intermediate variables on the dependent variable.

questions.q: What is the standard objective in an engineering optimisation application?
questions.a: To find a design or operating condition that maximises performance or minimises a specified quantity subject to the given conditions.
